## Trigger

When a lane is killed past its runner timeout and `commit.salvage` commits its worktree, I want the resulting commit subject to describe the bead's own work and type, so I can read `git log` and the changelog as an accurate record of what changed.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-06 landing `basicly-rupz`. Its lane hit the wall clock and `commit.salvage`
committed the worktree, which then merged to `main` verbatim as:

```
9607ff8 feat(runner): salvage the work a killed runner left uncommitted (basicly-rupz)
```

That subject describes `basicly-yvx9`'s feature - the salvage mechanism - not `rupz`'s work,
which was consuming the dispatch event stream. `commit.py:539` holds a module constant:

```python
SALVAGE_DESCRIPTION = "salvage the work a killed runner left uncommitted"
```

and `commit.py:596` passes it to `assemble` for every salvage, so every salvaged bead lands
under the same subject regardless of what it did.

## Why it is not cosmetic

The landing preserves individual commit subjects rather than squashing - `basicly-1lpo`
landed as `07f8c65 feat(supervise): fan a pass out over a label ...` because its salvage
refused and the commit was made by hand. So the wrong subject is permanent in `main`'s
history, and it is wrong on the two surfaces that read subjects as the record of what
changed: `git log` and the changelog fragment a lane writes.

It also mislabels the *type*. A salvage of a `docs`-only or `chore` bead still lands as
`feat(runner)`, so the subject asserts a scope and a type the diff does not support.

## Shape to consider

The bead title is already in hand at the salvage call site - `commit.salvage` takes `bead`.
Composing the subject from the bead's own title and type (the same source the
`conventional-commits` skill uses) makes the subject describe the work, and the salvage fact
belongs in the body, which `_salvage_body` already writes and a human already meets in
`git show`.

## Steps to Reproduce

Kill a metered lane past `runner_timeout` on any bead, let `commit.salvage` commit, then
read the subject: it names the salvage feature, not the bead.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: A salvaged commit's subject describes the bead's own work and carries the bead's own type and scope, not a fixed salvage description. The fact that a commit was a salvage is recorded in the commit body, not in the subject.

When a whole-repo reachability scan finds symbols with no production caller, some outright dead and some built but unwired despite being cited as a decision input in the docs, I want each one either wired to a real caller or deleted with its tests, so I can trust that a green dead-code gate means no unreferenced symbol remains.

## Context

Verified by whole-repo reachability scan over 594 non-binary files including catalog YAML, hooks, tests, docs and scripts.

Dead outright: `permissions.PERMISSION_TARGETS` (permissions.py:40) - exactly one occurrence repo-wide, its own definition. `policy.gate_from_unreliable_escalation` (policy.py:560) and its regex - tests only; tracked by the unreliable-escalation bead, delete here only if that bead resolves by dropping the offer. `PassSpendAdmission.unforecast` (supervise.py:1286) is always `()` from both constructors, so its UNBOUNDED coverage branch cannot fire. `cli.py:1756`'s `if args.usage_command != 'report'` guard is unreachable. `RunnerConfig.default_tier` (config.py:925) is stored but never read - `_apply_default_tier` already folds it onto every spec at load.

Built and unwired, cited by docs as a decision input: `run_record.landed_package_cost` (run_record.py:605) plus LandedCost and per_package - named as a prerequisite in architecture.md:1595, implementation-plan.md:447, agent-roster-design.md:218 and 459 and catalog-efficacy-design.md:385, but `basicly usage` exposes only report, forecast and tracker. Also `policy.should_escalate` (policy.py:485) - the n=2 rework predicate from §12.2, with callers instead comparing inline. Also `worktree.stale_sessions`.

Also here: the three renderer shims (renderers/claude.py, codex.py, copilot.py) are 11 lines each, byte-identical apart from a docstring, dispatched by importlib at cli.py:191 so invisible to the type checker. architecture.md:292 justifies the layer by per-target activation syntax that lives entirely in targets YAML and templates, not in these files.

## Trigger

When a declared scope glob matches a binary or very large tracked file, I want the working-set estimate to bound that file's contribution before it is decoded, so I can stop one large file from dominating a lane's size estimate.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import decompose
print(len(decompose._scope_files(Path('.'), ('.beads/**',))))
"
du -sh .beads
```

Observed - the glob matches the multi-hundred-megabyte tracker database and scope_read_cost reads it. Expected - a binary or oversized file contributes a bounded amount and does not dominate a lane's estimate.

## Context

`decompose.scope_read_cost` reads every matched file with `read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')`, and its docstring accepts this: binary content still counts by size via replacement. After the dependency and cache exclusion (basicly-jr0l.63) the remaining hazard is project-tracked binaries - most sharply `.beads/beads.db` plus its WAL and SHM, measured at 234 MB on this machine, which a scope of `**` or `.beads/**` will read fully into memory.

Deliberately left out of jr0l.63 to keep that diff to the stated defect. The fix is a size or binary guard rather than another directory name, because .beads is legitimate scope for a tracker-related bead.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given a declared scope matching a binary or very large file when the working set is estimated then that file does not dominate the estimate
- Given a declared scope matching ordinary source files when the working set is estimated then the figure is unchanged from before the guard

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: A file matched by a declared scope that is binary or very large contributes a bounded amount to the working-set estimate, and the bound applies before the file is fully read into memory. An ordinary source file's estimate stays at today's already-capped figure, not at a pre-cap baseline the tree no longer has.

## Trigger

When the rubric judge's metering is asserted only by a stubbed flag while the decider's metering is proven against real spend records, I want the same meter-level proof for the judge, so I can trust that every validated lane is actually metered rather than merely flagged as metered.

## Context

The four residual findings from the 2026-08-03 review of `basicly-gczc`, none blocking, grouped because they are all one theme: the judge half of that fix is asserted more weakly than the decider half, and three small claims are wider than what a test pins.

1. **The judge has no meter-level proof.** `tests/test_decisions.py` asserts `policy.spend_status(...).halted is False` over records the real `record_dispatch` wrote, plus a control that fails without the fix. The judge side asserts `seen['capture_usage'] is True` and stubs `record_dispatch` out entirely in its unwrap test. Per the rule the bead itself invoked - a passing parser is not evidence about a fail-open gate - the judge deserves the same assertion, and it matters more, because `rubrics.evaluate` runs on **every** validated lane while the decider runs only on a delegated decision.

2. **`basicly runner dry-run` prints an argv a real dispatch would not send.** `cli.py:3525` does not pass `capture_usage`, so the printed command omits the usage flags a metered dispatch appends. Harmless to metering, but `runner.py:226` claims every command is printable via `runner dry-run`, and this one is printable as something else.

3. **Two documented branches of the new code have no test.** `_claude_result_field`'s `isinstance(value, str)` guard is justified in prose by an `is_error` envelope carrying a structured payload under `result`, and no test passes a non-string `result` - the existing case only covers the key being absent. `_codex_agent_message`'s tolerance of a truncated final line is likewise asserted in prose only.

4. **Two tests key on a literal token appearing in a comment.** `tests/test_decisions.py` and `tests/test_rubrics.py` use `inspect.getsource` to require the string `capture_usage` in nearby prose. They do discriminate - both fail on revert - but a future reword to 'usage capture' fails them for no behavioural reason. Acceptable given the defect class they guard (a comment asserting a property the code lacked), so this is a recorded coupling rather than a defect: decide deliberately whether to keep it.

Reviewer coverage boundary, recorded so it is not assumed away: no agent CLI was invoked during that review, so the probe figures in `b512487`'s message were not independently reproduced, and the codex `item.completed`/`agent_message` shape rests on the earlier probe pinned in `tests/test_runner.py`.

- `tests/test_rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_runner.py`

## Trigger

When the path-restore form of `git checkout`, plus `git restore` and `git stash`, can discard uncommitted work with nothing refusing them, I want a mechanical deny rule for that family beside the other destructive-command backstops, so I can stop losing edits to a command the rules already name but do not block.

## The failure this comes from

I ran `git checkout HEAD -- tests/test_cli.py` during basicly-vkh0.42 and lost two of my
own uncommitted edits. Nothing refused it. The `require-explicit-confirmation` fragment
names the family in as many words, and the permissions comment
(`.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml:34`) names these three commands *specifically*
as undenied — so the rule was written, read and still not followed.

**Root cause: the rule lives only in prose, and prose is advisory at the moment of the
call.** Every neighbouring family in that file has a mechanical backstop —
`destructive-rm`, `destructive-git`, `bypass-gates`, `force-push`. This one has a comment
explaining why it does not. The asymmetry is what made it the family that got through.

## The control

A `destructive-restore` deny entry beside `destructive-git`:

```yaml
  - id: destructive-restore
    description: block path-restore and stash, which discard uncommitted work silently
    claude:
      - "Bash(git checkout --*)"
      - "Bash(git checkout*--*)"
      - "Bash(git restore*)"
      - "Bash(git stash*)"
    copilot:
      - "shell(git restore)"
      - "shell(git stash)"
```

`git checkout <branch>` and `git checkout -b` stay allowed, which is what the loop's own
branch handling needs. The engine drives git through `subprocess`, not through the Bash
tool, so no deny rule reaches it — verify that before landing rather than assuming it.

Then rewrite the comment at lines 33-37: it currently teaches the reader that these three
are undenied, which will be false.

**Editing the permissions catalog is on the confirmation list.** This record is the
proposal; a human disposes of it.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml`
- `.claude/settings.json`
- `tests/test_permissions.py`

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given the projected `.claude/settings.json` when it is read then it carries a deny rule
  matching `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore` and `git stash`
- Given `git checkout -b <name>` and `git checkout <branch>` when either is attempted then
  neither is denied, proven by a matcher probe rather than by inspection
- Given `permissions-check` when it runs then it passes with the new entry projected

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The projected `.claude/settings.json` carries a deny rule matching the path-restore form of `git checkout`, plus `git restore` and `git stash`. Checking out an existing branch by name, or creating one with `-b`, stays allowed, proven by a matcher probe rather than by inspection. `permissions-check` passes with the new entry projected, and the permissions comment no longer claims these commands are undenied.

## Trigger

When a scripted multi-line regex reports the right match count but deletes far more lines than intended, I want the `non-interactive-shell` fragment to require a line-delta check after a scripted in-place edit, so I can catch a wrong-sized match that a site count alone cannot see.

## The failure this comes from

A multi-line regex I ran over `tests/test_decompose.py` during basicly-vkh0.42 removed
**1644 lines**. The pattern was `(?:    .*
)+?(?=

)`, intended to cut one indented
block; the lazy quantifier still spanned every blank-line-separated run in the file. The
module was restored from HEAD and every edit reapplied by hand.

## Why the existing rule did not catch it

The `non-interactive-shell` fragment already says to name the expected site count before a
scripted multi-site replace and reconcile after. It did not bind here, for two reasons:

- **A deletion's site count was right.** One match, as predicted. The match was the wrong
  *size*, and a count of matches cannot see size.
- The rule reads as being about replacement, so an edit framed as a cut does not obviously
  fall under it.

## The control

Extend that fragment with the magnitude clause: after any scripted in-place edit, compare
`wc -l` before and against after, and name the expected delta first. A delta larger than
the change described is a stop, the same way a site-count delta is. One line, in the
fragment that already carries the site-count rule, so it lands in every agent's always-on
baseline — check the character budget before adding, since that baseline is at its cap.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/fragments/non-interactive-shell.yaml`

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given the `non-interactive-shell` fragment when it is read then it names the line-delta
  reconciliation for a scripted in-place edit, distinct from the site-count rule
- Given the projected instruction files when `basicly check` runs then every per-target
  character cap still passes

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The `non-interactive-shell` fragment names a line-delta reconciliation step for a scripted in-place edit, distinct from the existing site-count rule. Every projected instruction file still passes its per-target character cap after the addition.

## Trigger

When the local toolchain and continuous integration resolve different versions of `uv`, node and git with nothing declaring an expected version, I want a declared version or range per tool checked on both sides, so I can stop a gate from passing or failing depending on which machine ran it.

## The defect

The repository declares one toolchain floor, `requires-python = ">=3.14"`, and pins nothing else. Continuous integration floats `uv` to latest and pins node to an older major than this machine runs, so a gate can pass locally and fail in continuous integration, or the reverse, and no measurement would say which.

Measured 2026-08-19.

| tool | this machine | continuous integration | direction of skew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| uv | 0.11.28 | unpinned, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` resolves latest, which is 0.12.5 released 2026-08-14 | local **behind** |
| node | 24.18.0 | `node-version: 22` in two workflows | local **ahead** by two majors |
| git | 2.43.0, and the distribution candidate is also 2.43.0 | `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, whatever that image ships | local behind, by an unmeasured amount |
| python | 3.14.6 | resolved by uv from `requires-python` | local behind 3.14.7, released 2026-08-05 |

## Why this is a defect rather than housekeeping

A behaviour difference between the two is already demonstrable. `uv init` gained a default build system in uv 0.12.0, released 2026-08-28... corrected: released 2026-07-28. So the same command produces a different project layout on this machine than in continuous integration, today. `uv init --help` on 0.11.28 lists both `--package` and `--no-package`, so a flag probe does not reveal it and only running the command does.

The repository is a distribution installed into other repositories, so its own gates are the product. A gate whose outcome depends on an unpinned tool version is a gate whose outcome nobody can reproduce.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `uv --version` locally and read 0.11.28.
2. Read `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` and `basicly.yml` and observe `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` with no version input.
3. Fetch the current uv release and observe 0.12.5.
4. Read `node-version: 22` in both workflows and compare with `node --version` locally, 24.18.0.
5. Observe that no file in the tree states a version for uv, node or git.

Observed: three tools skew in two directions and nothing declares an expected version.
Expected: the toolchain a gate runs on is declared, and a difference is visible rather than latent.

## The decision this needs, recorded rather than assumed

Whether to pin continuous integration to the local toolchain, or to raise the local toolchain to what continuous integration resolves, or to declare a floor and a ceiling per tool and check both. This record does not choose. What it refuses is the current state, where neither side is declared.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `.scripts/`
- `tests/`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: A declared version or range answers, per tool, what continuous integration and a local run expect for `uv`, node and git. Continuous integration provisions the declared version instead of resolving latest. A local toolchain outside the declared range is reported rather than passing silently, and a new tool release does not fail anything until a human widens the range.

## Trigger

When the factory loop's states, gates and artifacts fall short of what the architecture document specifies, I want this epic decomposed and built against that specification, so I can drive a unit of work through every state with a gate binding at each boundary.

## Context

The loop is specified in prose across `docs/design/factory-design.md`, the agent roster design and
the `harness-loop` skill. The engine implements a smaller, different thing. Measured 2026-08-07 by
a line-by-line read: **the loop is a two-state machine wearing seven labels** — real enforcement
happens at build→verify, and every other boundary is a checkpoint or a lint.

The full delta, the decisions taken, the research behind them and the open questions are
externalised in `docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md`. That document is the input to this
epic, and this epic is how it gets built.

**This epic dogfoods its own subject.** It is decomposed and driven through the loop it specifies,
so each state's gaps are felt while the state is being built.

Headline measured gaps, each with evidence in the requirements document:

- decompose emits no dependency graph; ordering is derived from scope overlap only
- validate never runs for plain leaves, and its only deterministic check is re-running verify
- SHIPPED 2026-08-08 (basicly-u2hl.4): repair now runs in the lane's own worktree, briefed with
  the gate's actual findings
- CI gates guard two boundaries of six as of 2026-08-08 (basicly-u2hl.1 added the plan gate on
  entry to BUILD, alongside build->verify)
- zero of seven personas are implemented
- retrospective does not exist in the engine

## Trigger

When a unit enters loop intake, I want the loop to emit a solution design carrying five machine-checked sections, so I can dispute the requirement before the unit reaches classify.

## Context

Requirements doc D17 and section 8.1. INTAKE today records **one enum value** - `loop._on_intake`
calls `classify.classify(repo, id, work_type)` and that is the whole artifact.

Five sections, machine-checked, markdown not JSON (the `## Plan` section and
`needs-input.json` are the two proven precedents here):

```text
## Problem            the requirement in the requester's terms
## Success            an observable, not a feeling
## Consumer transcript  the command as it will be typed, and what it prints
## Out of scope       what this deliberately does not do
## Constraints        what the solution may not violate
```

## Why a transcript and not a mockup

This product has no screens. Its consumer surface is the CLI, `basicly.toml`, the catalog
schemas, the generated-file contract and the ledger format. The transcript does a mockup's
job: a reader disputes the surface before it exists, the agent receives the exact strings it
must produce, and the `quality-gate` fragment's existing rule - exercise the change as it
will really be used - checks the same thing from the shipping end.

## Ratchet

Follow `basicly-u2hl.1`: bind on the presence of the heading block, so beads filed before
this exists are admitted and one that carries the block incompletely is refused naming the
section. Do not bulk-transform the 667 existing beads.

## Trigger

When `basicly install` runs against a repository that selects copilot, I want the resolved tier written into copilot's per-subagent config, so I can pin a copilot subagent spawn without putting a model id in the agent file.

## Context

Re-probed 2026-08-09 against copilot CLI 1.0.78. The tier kit's copilot installer installs
nothing and explains that copilot "exposes no hook surface that fires for a spawn, so its
working path is static frontmatter plus copilot --model". Both halves of that explanation are
now false:

- copilot ships hooks, including one that intercepts a subagent finishing **before its results
  return to the parent** (`.github/hooks/*.json`, plus inline definitions in config)
- copilot carries per-subagent selection in **config**, at
  `subagents.agents.<name>.{model, effortLevel, contextTier}`, configurable with `/subagents`

The second is the load-bearing one. It means a copilot spawn is pinnable **without a
frontmatter `model`**, which is exactly what D30 requires and what the installer currently
reports as impossible.

## Scope

- Resolve the declared tier through the D31 vendor walk and write the result into copilot's
  per-subagent config at install time, not into the agent file.
- The installer stops reporting a no-op for copilot and reports what it wrote.
- `effortLevel` and `contextTier` have no equivalent in our tier vocabulary. Decide whether
  they are derived from the tier, declared separately, or deliberately left unset - and record
  which, because an unset field on a multi-vendor surface is a silent default.

## Constraint

No provider model id in any agent file, generated or not (D30). The projected `.agent.md` must
stay model-free; the resolved id lives in config, which is generated and rewritten on install.

## Correction already landed

The stale explanation is corrected in the `tier-injection` skill in place rather than left
beside the new claim, and it names this bead as the fix.

## Demonstration

Install into a scratch repo, then show the generated copilot config carrying the resolved model
for a `tier: low` agent while `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` carries no model line.

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given an agent declaring `tier: low` when `basicly install` runs against a repo whose
  selection includes copilot then the generated copilot config carries the tier resolved
  through the D31 vendor walk at `subagents.agents.<name>.model`, and
  `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` carries no `model` line - which is D30 held on the surface
  it constrains.
- Given the tier kit's copilot installer runs then it reports what it wrote to config, and no
  longer reports that a spawn cannot be pinned - the stale reason it prints today
  (`.basicly/core/kit/tier/install_hook.py`, the `"copilot"` entry, "no copilot hook is known
  to fire for a spawn ... frontmatter plus `copilot --model` instead") is gone rather than
  left beside the new claim.
- Given `effortLevel` and `contextTier`, which have no equivalent in this repo's tier
  vocabulary, then the decision to derive them from the tier, declare them separately or
  leave them unset is recorded with its reason - an unset field on a multi-vendor surface is a
  silent default, so it must be a stated one.
- Given `basicly install` runs twice with the same selection then the second run leaves the
  copilot config byte-identical, matching the convergence the kit already claims for the
  hook path.
- Given a repo whose selection excludes copilot then no copilot config is written and no
  copilot line is reported.
- Given the vendor facts this rests on were probed against copilot CLI 1.0.78 on 2026-08-09
  then the implementation re-probes the live surface before writing the config path, and
  records the version it probed - the claim being replaced was stale precisely because it
  pinned no version.
- Demonstrated by: install into a scratch repo, then show the generated copilot config
  carrying the resolved model for a `tier: low` agent while `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md`
  carries no model line.

## Trigger

When a grant sits on an epic and one of its children reaches the ship checkpoint, I want `loop advance` to accept a `--root` naming the epic, so I can reach the same grant the supervised path already reaches.

## Context

Found 2026-08-15 while verifying the `basicly-u2hl.56` fix by hand.

`_on_verify` now resolves the ship checkpoint through `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded`
with `ctx.grant_root`. The supervisor passes `session.root_issue`, so the supervised path
reaches the grant. `basicly loop advance` accepts no `--root`, so `ctx.grant_root` is None
and the guarded call defaults to the issue itself - which carries no grant when the grant is
on the epic.

Observed - `basicly loop advance basicly-b2n2` returns
`[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval` while
`basicly loop preflight basicly-u2hl` reports `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates
it`, because the grant is on `basicly-u2hl` and nothing tells `advance` so.

This is not the same defect as `u2hl.56`, which was the parked path not asking at all. This
is the hand path having no way to say which session it belongs to. `loop run` already takes
`--root` for exactly this.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the two surfaces side by side - this alone establishes the defect:

       uv run basicly loop advance --help
       uv run basicly loop run --help

   Observed 2026-08-19: `loop run` carries
   `--root ROOT   Session root issue whose autonomy grant may cover the checkpoints
   (default: the issue itself)`, and `loop advance` carries no `--root` at all - its options
   are `--work-type`, `--children`, `--mode`, `--runner`, `--autonomy` and nothing else.
2. Put an L3 grant on an epic and take one of its children to the ship checkpoint.
3. Ask the hand path to advance the child:

       uv run basicly loop advance <child-id>

4. Ask the preflight, on the epic, whether the grant covers that same ship:

       uv run basicly loop preflight <epic-id>

5. Read the code path that explains the disagreement:

       rg -n 'approve_checkpoint_guarded' src/basicly/loop.py
       rg -n 'grant_root' src/basicly/cli.py

Observed - this record's measurement 2026-08-15, verifying the `basicly-u2hl.56` fix by hand:
step 3 returned

    [blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval

while step 4 reported `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it`. `_on_verify` resolves
the ship checkpoint through `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded` with `ctx.grant_root`; the
supervisor passes `session.root_issue` and so reaches the grant, but `loop advance` accepts no
`--root`, so `ctx.grant_root` is None and the guarded call defaults to the issue itself -
which carries no grant, because the grant is on the epic.

Expected: `loop advance` takes `--root` with the same meaning and default `loop run` already
gives it, so the hand path can name the session it belongs to and reaches the same grant the
supervised path does. This is not `basicly-u2hl.56`, which was the parked path not asking at
all; this is the hand path having no way to say which session it is in.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given a grant on an epic and a child at the ship checkpoint when `basicly loop advance
  <child> --root <epic>` runs then the checkpoint is approved under that grant and the
  advance proceeds, rather than blocking on human approval.
- Given `basicly loop advance <child>` with no `--root` then the behaviour is unchanged, so
  the default stays the issue itself and nothing silently widens.
- Given `basicly loop advance --help` then `--root` is described in the same terms
  `loop run --help` uses, because two spellings of one concept is what this record is about.
- Given a `--root` naming a record that carries no grant then the advance blocks and says the
  named root carries no grant, rather than reporting the child's own absence of one.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run basicly loop advance <child> --root <epic>` advancing past the ship
  checkpoint, against a control run without `--root` on the same record that still blocks.

## Trigger

When a caller writes a folded field event whose value exceeds a declared producer bound, I want the write refused at the seam with the field named, so I can drop what is derivable instead of storing an unbounded payload.

## The defect

`basicly-vbl35a` made the cap stop cutting any key the fold reads, which acceptance criterion 1 required. The consequence it names rather than buries: `field`.`value` and every `created` payload key are now stored **whole** where `value` was previously cut at 4096 bytes, and **nothing in the tree bounds them**.

That is not a regression against the old behaviour for `created` — a description under `description` was always uncapped, and 31 are stored above 4096 with the largest at 7043. It **is** a new hole for `field`.`value`, which the cap did bound, wrongly, and now bounds not at all.

The reason the cap exists is section 32.10 first paragraph: git compression, the ship-time rollup and a change-sized write all assume bounded events, and none of them bounds a single pasted payload. An agent that pastes a multi-megabyte log into a description now puts it in every clone, compressed and unremovable, because true removal is the history rewrite section 32.8 forbids.

## Why the cap cannot be the answer

Cutting a folded field makes a derived value depend on the cap, which breaks the determinism section 32.2 asserts. So the bound has to move to the **producer**, which is D-36 derivability argument applied to a field rather than to an artifact: a body is bounded by dropping what the ledger can already derive, not by a byte count.

`basicly-gvlpxm` does exactly this for `change-summary`. It does not cover a folded field, so this record is the sibling case and not a duplicate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a field event whose value is a 5 MB string through the engine seam.
2. Read the stored event. Observe the whole 5 MB, no truncation flag, and no refusal.
3. Confirm no gate refuses it: run the verify suite and observe every check pass.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/`

When an existing oversized value is already in the log, the fold derives the same state and nothing rewrites it.

When migrate renders a payload for comparison, I want it to name the kind it is rendering instead of relying on the kind-blind default, so I can make the divergence comparison exact by construction rather than by coincidence.

## Context

`migrate.py` calls `prepare_payload` with no `kind`, and `_text_bound` answers `(None, None)` for that case: cut at nothing, refused at nothing. It agrees with `append` **today** only because it renders a `created` payload, and `created` stores whole on both sides. Change either side and the divergence comparison silently compares a whole payload against a cut one. Passing `kind=events.KIND_CREATED` makes it exact by construction.

## Trigger

When live worktrees already exist, I want the preflight forecast to price the lane count provisioning would actually seed, so I can size a grant against what a pass can really run rather than against the raw concurrency cap.

## Context

`loop preflight` forecasts a pass at `per_lane x min(concurrency, open_children)`.
Provisioning does not use `concurrency`; `loop._ensure_child_worktrees` computes
`room = wt_config.concurrency - len(existing)` and seeds at most that many. So the
forecast over-states by exactly the number of worktrees already live.

Measured 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz`, with 2 live worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

```
worktrees: 2 live
forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))
```

The pass can seed 3 lanes, not 5. The honest forecast is ~66,569,541.

## Why the size of the error matters rather than the error

The figure exists to size a grant. An operator reading 110,949,235 against a
100,000,000 grant concludes the pass cannot run and either mints a larger grant than
the work needs or does not run it. Both were nearly done here. `admit_pass_spend`
totals the pass and refuses the whole thing on one violation, so the number a human
compares against the grant is the number that decides whether anything is dispatched
at all.

The preflight's own docstring states the intent — "the interesting number is what a
*full* fan-out would need, because that is what a budget has to be minted for" — and a
full fan-out is bounded by room, not by the cap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the cap and count the worktrees already live:

       rg -n '^concurrency' basicly.toml
       git worktree list

2. Read the two expressions that have to agree, and observe that they do not.
   `cli._print_preflight_spend` prices `priced = min(cap, open_count)` on the line it
   prints as `forecast:`; provisioning computes `room = wt_config.concurrency -
   len(existing)` in `loop._ensure_child_worktrees`. Nothing subtracts `len(existing)`
   on the forecast path.
3. Run the forecast on a root with open children but no dispatchable lane - that is the
   only branch which prints it, because `_print_preflight_spend` returns early as soon as
   `supervise.ready_lanes` is non-empty:

       uv run basicly loop preflight <root>

4. Read the `forecast:` line, then multiply its `per-lane:` figure by the room from step 1
   by hand and compare.

Observed - this record's own measurement, 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz` with 2 live
worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

    worktrees: 2 live
    forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))

The pass could seed 3 lanes; the honest figure was ~66,569,541. Re-checked in this checkout
2026-08-19: `git worktree list` shows **4** lane worktrees against `concurrency = 5`, so
room is 1 while the forecast would still price 5 - the inputs have made the error larger,
not smaller.

Expected: the forecast prices the room provisioning would use, and its parenthetical names
room rather than the raw cap.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given live worktrees exist when the preflight forecasts a pass then the lane count
  is the room provisioning would use rather than the raw cap - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
- Given no live worktrees then the forecast is unchanged - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Trigger

When the harness still needs an external tracker binary for phase derivation, gates, checkpoints, and dependency edges, I want the tracker to own its state end to end, so I can run a full factory session and a fresh consumer install with no external binary on the path.

## Context

Opened 2026-07-25 on the owner's direction. The tracker is not a peripheral integration - it is the harness's state. br is the single source of truth for every phase derivation, gate, checkpoint, dependency edge, decision item and run record, and the engine deliberately keeps no side-state, so every guarantee the harness makes is downstream of it. That dependency is unowned: beads_rust and bv are MIT and excellent today, but licenses change, maintainers move on, and a breaking change upstream lands in our critical path. We already carry a version floor and version-specific workarounds.

Design doc: docs/work-tracker.md, opened as an initialization rather than a build plan. The tractable part is that the harness's tracker surface is narrow and enumerable - roughly twenty subcommands - so this is not rebuilding a general-purpose issue tracker. Telemetry comes first: no schema is designed from memory of our own usage.

## Success Criteria

- No process the engine starts spawns an external tracker binary, and the mode set names exactly one mode: `src/basicly/owned_store.py` has `TRACKER_MODES = (MODE_OWNED,)` and `src/basicly/tracker.py` re-exports it (checked 2026-08-19). Owner clarification 2026-08-13 (`basicly-ctdz`): the criterion is absence from the runtime path, not deletion of `br`/`bv` support, which other projects use.
- A fresh consumer repository installs basicly and drives a record to shipped with no external binary on `PATH`. `basicly-vkh0.49` (the terminal repository) is that test and `basicly-vkh0.48` is the same proof for the development workspace; neither has run, so this epic's acceptance is unmet whatever the child count says. 47 of 60 children are closed as of 2026-08-19.
- The ledger is the only store: `.beads/` is absent from `main` (checked 2026-08-19), and the kit's own entry point - `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py` with `fsck` and `rebuild` - reproduces the fold from the log with no basicly import and nothing on `PATH`.
- A write reports its own outcome truthfully. `basicly-vkh0.50` is open - the write seam prints `recorded:` and exits 0 whether or not the write landed - so until it closes, no criterion on this epic may be verified from that line; the field is read back instead.
- The store can remove a record and cannot silently lose one: `basicly-vkh0.34` (neither store can remove a record), `basicly-b2n2` (a stale auto-flush deletes committed records) and `basicly-dx2ngn` (the shrink guard is inert on the rebuild path) each close with a test that fails when the guard is made inert.
- The surface list is frozen on a current usage sample rather than the 2026-07 one (`basicly-vkh0.47`). The shadow differential that justified the flip left with the external half, so the flip's evidence is the record it wrote, not a command anyone can re-run - any further claim about store agreement needs a new instrument, named on the child that makes it.

## Scope

- `docs/work-tracker.md`

## Trigger

When every lane in a supervised pass appends tracker events to one shared ledger file, I want each lane to write its own segment instead, so I can drop the undeclared-append-only-path advisory without serialising every plan on a path nobody declared.

## Context

basicly loop preflight prints an advisory every pass: no append-only path declared, a path every lane writes is invisible to the grouping until it is listed. The path is .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl - every lane writes tracker events, they mirror into the owned ledger, and the ledger is committed.

Declaring it in [worktree] append_only_paths is the wrong remedy. That list is empty on purpose: its own comment records that CHANGELOG.md was the whole list and that serializing every lane was the cost of detecting a collision the repo created for itself. decompose serializes every child that does not declare the path and call it shared, and no bead declares it, so declaring it today serializes every plan.

The ledger already has the same shape available - events.LOG_GLOB folds every events-*.jsonl, snapshot.rotate exists and has no caller, and the lexicographic ordering rule is written down. A per-lane segment would make the log a set of files no two lanes share, so nothing contends and the advisory disappears because the fact behind it is gone.

Open question the build must answer: whether a segment is per lane or per period, and how a segment name sorts against the year-period rotation names the kit already reserves.

## Trigger

When a harness surface still names the retired external tracker binary or its directory, I want every surface purged and the directory deleted, so I can guarantee no printed instruction, help text or commit gate depends on a binary no checkout has.

## Context

Removing the external binary from the engine is basicly-wpc8 and basicly-vkh0.29. This epic is the other half nobody had filed: every harness surface that still names the binary or its directory, and the deletion of that directory at the end.

The inventory was taken 2026-08-17 with a probe that excludes the mermaid line-break noise a naive word search picks up, `(^|[^a-z<-])br [a-z][a-z-]+`, over tracked files only. Counts of real invocations: the catalog sources 127 in 13 files, the projected skills 96 in 5 files, the documents 32 in 8 files, the config 7 in 1, the scripts 6 in 2, the workflows 1 in 1.

## The one that must move first

The commit gate does **not** spawn the binary. `.basicly/core/hooks/beads-commit-msg.py` validates the trailing id against `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is a file read. So the gate depends on the export file rather than the binary, and if the directory is deleted before the gate is repointed, every commit in this repository fails. That is child 1, and the deletion child blocks on it.

## What is deliberately not here

- The config, `basicly.toml`. It is inside basicly-vkh0.29's declared scope, and two beads declaring one file is a contention the plan gate should never be handed.
- `src/basicly/worktree.py` and the `.beads/redirect` filename. Architecture section 37.2 records that the filename is the binary's and changes at the flip, and that module is inside basicly-wpc8's scope.
- `br.PINNED_VERSION`. It leaves with `br.py` itself.
- The nine records with no body in the owned ledger. That is basicly-vkh0.41, and it is a precondition of the deletion rather than a surface.

## Sizing, measured

Four children are lane-sized and three are below the working-set band floor of 8000, which by basicly-esxp's rule makes them session work rather than a lane: the commit gate at 4152, the workflows at 5523, the deletion at 5019. Sized with `read_cost.scope_read_cost` times the task factor of 3.

## Order

Children 1 to 6 are independent of each other. The deletion is last and blocks on all of them, on basicly-vkh0.41 and on basicly-vkh0.29.

## Success Criteria

- The purge this epic was named for is discharged. Checked 2026-08-19: `.beads/` is absent from the tree, `src/basicly/owned_store.py` has `TRACKER_MODES = (MODE_OWNED,)`, and eleven of fifteen children are closed including the deletion child (`basicly-vkh0.42.7`) and every surface child. The four open children are the requirements-folder work, which is a new gate and two deletions rather than a purge.
- No surface a user reads names a command from the retired binary. Not yet true: `src/basicly/cli.py` prints `cover each: br dep add <root> <id> -t blocks` from `basicly loop preflight`, and six `--help` descriptions in the same module still say "a br gate", "child br issues", "br work type" and "pure read over br" (checked 2026-08-19). The criterion is zero occurrences in printed strings and in `--help` text, under a probe that separates those populations from docstring prose - 122 residue hits across `src/` and `.basicly/core/` under `(^|[^a-z<-])br [a-z][a-z-]+` are overwhelmingly prose, so a raw count is not the instrument.

- Every citation of a deleted requirements document resolves after the absorption, and the two gates that read those documents - repointed by `basicly-vkh0.42.8`, closed - stay green.

## Trigger

When `basicly loop preflight` and five `--help` strings still instruct the operator to run the retired external tracker binary, I want that printed and help text corrected, so I can follow a remediation instruction that names a command the current checkout actually has.

## The defect

`basicly loop preflight` prints a remediation line instructing the operator to run a command that cannot run. `src/basicly/cli.py` line 2931:

```
print(f"           cover each: br dep add {state.root_issue} <id> -t blocks")
```

The binary is gone from every checkout, so this is a consumer facing instruction that fails whoever follows it. Five more surfaces carry the same name in text a consumer reads, all in the same module: the verify help at 4402 and 4415, the decompose help at 4462, the scaffold help at 4535, the classify help at 4651.

`basicly-e2mz.44` is closed and covered a different thing, the seam **argument grammar** that a human types. This is the engine printing the retired name back at the operator.

## The population, and why a raw count is the wrong instrument

A search for the binary name across the engine and the catalog returns 122 hits and **the overwhelming majority are docstring prose**, which is history and correctly left alone. Only text a consumer reads is a defect: a printed line, a help string, an error message. Split the population before editing, name the expected count per population, and reconcile after. A sweep that treated 122 as a defect count is how a previous removal left four false user facing messages in the tree.

1. Run `basicly loop preflight` on a root whose blockers are not all covered, so the remediation branch is reached.
2. Read the printed line. Observe it instructs a `dep add` through the retired binary.

4. Run `basicly loop preflight --help`, `basicly verify --help`, `basicly decompose --help`, `basicly policy scaffold --help` and `basicly loop run --help`. Observe five help strings naming the binary.
5. Positive control for the population split: the same search finds the name in docstrings, and those are history rather than defects, so a raw count over the tree does not answer this.

## Trigger

When the importer still copies `created_by` and `assignee` into the ledger payload, I want it to drop identity-bearing fields on the write path, so I can stop a repository several machines write to from accumulating an identity no single machine's gate can see.

## Context

Two committed and pushed files carry a person's username and a personal e-mail address. Architecture §32.7 claimed absolutely that no committed artifact carries a username, and the claim is false.

Measured 2026-08-17, twice by paths sharing no step — a field-wise count over the parsed records and a raw-line regex over the bytes — and both agree on the substance:

    .beads/issues.jsonl, 924 records
      created_by: <redacted:machine-username> 846, <redacted:machine-username> 78
      assignee:   niksavis@live.com 56, <redacted:machine-username> 26
      lines holding an e-mail address: 58

    .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl, 5616 lines
      lines holding an e-mail address: 59
      lines holding the redaction placeholder: 4944   <- positive control, the rule does fire

Both files are tracked, committed and pushed to a public remote, so this is published rather than merely present.

## Why every gate is green over it

`tracker-path-scan` builds its identity rule from `getpass.getuser()`, which on this machine is `<redacted:machine-username>`. The identity in the stores is a **different** one. So the gate is not broken and its green result is correct — it is answering "does this artifact carry *your* identity" when the requirement is "does it carry *anyone's*".

That is the general defect, and it is worth stating separately from the data: an identity gate keyed on the running user cannot see another user's identity, and a repository that several machines write to will accumulate identities no single machine's gate can find.

## What is bounded and what is not

Every identity-bearing event in the owned ledger carries the import's own source marker; no live write path produces one. So the population is inherited from the pre-cutover import and is not growing. That bounds the remedy to a backfill plus a format rule — it does not make the published values unpublished.

## The three remedies, and which needs an owner

Removing the values from the current files is a corrective append or a rewrite, and the rewrite of a committed append-only log is the exception architecture §4.2 reserves for an explicit owner decision. Removing them from **history** is a force-push, which is an owner decision of a different order and is not this bead's to take. Preventing the next one is the format rule and the deny-list configuration, which is ordinary work.

Note the deny-list the hook already names, `[[privacy.denied]]`, belongs in the gitignored `basicly.local.toml` — 787 bytes, all comments, parsing to an empty table. The mechanism exists and was never configured.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Count the identity-bearing lines in the committed store, with the redaction placeholder
   as the control that proves the rule fires at all:

       git grep -c -E '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}' HEAD -- .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl
       git grep -c '<redacted:machine-username>' HEAD -- .
       grep -c 'redacted:' .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl

2. Run the gate that is supposed to catch this and read its result:

       uv run pre-commit run tracker-path-scan --all-files

3. Read why that result is green, which is the general defect:

       rg -n 'getpass|getuser' .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py

4. Check whether the deny-list the hooks already name was ever configured:

       rg -n 'privacy.denied' basicly.local.toml
       wc -c basicly.local.toml
       rg -n 'privacy.*denied' .basicly/core/hooks/internal-info-scan.py

   Observed 2026-08-19: the first command returns nothing, `basicly.local.toml` is **787
   bytes and every line of it is a comment**, and the third command is the **positive
   control** - `internal-info-scan.py` reads `data.get("privacy", {}).get("denied", [])`
   out of exactly that file, and `tracker-path-scan.py` names the same list. So the
   mechanism exists, reads this file, and was never configured; the empty result is a
   missing configuration rather than a missing feature.

Observed, re-measured 2026-08-19 in this checkout: the ledger holds 6027 lines, **61** of
them carrying an e-mail address and **213** carrying the username `<redacted:machine-username>`, and `git grep`
finds `<redacted:machine-username>` in that one file and nowhere else in the tree - so the values are committed
at HEAD, not merely present in a working copy. **The positive control is the third command**,
which returns **4955** lines carrying the redaction placeholder: the rule does fire, over the
same bytes, on the great majority of records. So the 61 and the 213 are a population the rule
missed rather than a probe that failed.

Step 3 shows why: `tracker-path-scan` builds its identity rule from `getpass.getuser()`, so
it asks "does this artifact carry *your* identity" where the requirement is "does it carry
*anyone's*". The gate is not broken and its green result is correct - the rule is the wrong
question. An identity gate keyed on the running user cannot see another user's identity, and
a repository several machines write to accumulates identities no single machine's gate can
find.

**One of the two stores this record was filed over is gone.** `.beads/issues.jsonl` and its
924 records are no longer in the tree or in git's index - `git ls-files .beads` returns
nothing - so the 846/78 `created_by` and 56/26 `assignee` counts in the Context above are
history rather than a current reading, and `docs/architecture` §32.7.1 ("two stores carry
another") is itself now one store out of date. The owned ledger half above stands and is the
live population.

Expected: the format rule refuses an identity-bearing field on the write path whoever the
running user is; the inherited values are removed from the current file by the corrective
route architecture §4.2 reserves for an append-only log; and the architecture claim is
restated to match what is measurable.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py`
- `src/basicly/redact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/internal-info-scan.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`
- `tests/test_br_scrub_ledger.py`

payload.value: The importer copies no identity-bearing field into a record's payload and names every field it dropped. A scan reports a store holding an identity the running-user rule cannot match against a configured deny list, and names the rule that matched; it stays inert with a stated reason when no deny list is configured. A record already carrying a bare identity is corrected by an append, never a history rewrite or a silent edit.

## Trigger

When the outcome-routing section of `supervise.py` carries zero inbound edges and the largest prose share of any section, I want it extracted into its own module, so I can shrink `supervise.py` without adding a forwarding shim or raising either size gate's baseline.

## Context

Found by the lane-B survey 2026-08-14, with a measured dependency scan. `basicly-tcmy.13` owns the split. This names where to cut.

Cross-section edge counts, from an abstract syntax tree walk between the section headers:

```text
section                 lines        inbound edges    prose share
lock and heartbeat      108-310      2                36.9%
outcome routing         2810-3905    0                45.2%
usage meter             978-1158     1                34.2%
telemetry and dispatch  2077-2809    6                48.5%
```

## Why routing goes first

It is a pure dependency sink. Zero inbound references means no symbol in `supervise` needs a forwarding shim. It consumes only the lane outcome, the session state, the found-info record, the ready set, and the `merge`, `loop`, `decisions` and `policy` modules.

After the cycle is thinned, the meter at 978-1158 is the only thing `loop` reaches in `supervise`. Extracting it is what removes the layering exemption.

Routing at 45.2% prose sits above the module mean of 43.6%, so extracting it lowers the remainder's share. Both sides sit under the cap on a line-based measure. Re-measure with the gate's own token-based script before the commit, because `supervise.py` is frozen at 55.9.

`tests/test_supervise.py` is frozen at 60,132 tokens. Move the routing tests out with the code or the test module's own ratchet blocks the lane.

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`

The thinning of the loop to supervise cycle.

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py -q`, both ratchet scripts, and `uv run lint-imports`.

## Trigger

When a Claude lane still dispatches as a subprocess `claude -p` invocation with no per-subagent usage record, I want same-vendor lanes dispatched through the host runtime as real subagents, so I can observe per-subagent spend and satisfy the hybrid dispatch shape the owner decided.

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
**The title is refuted as written.** "Instead of spawning a headless CLI" cannot be delivered:
the Python Agent SDK (`claude-agent-sdk`) drives the installed CLI as a local subprocess -
`CLINotFoundError` and its own transport documentation say so. What changes is **how a
definition is loaded**, not whether a subprocess exists. Restate as: *spawn the role definition
as a subagent so its declared `skills:` preload and per-subagent usage is emitted.*

**A third of the text below argues a settled point.** The section "The decision this
contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident" attacks `agent-roster-design.md:210`
and `factory-loop-requirements.md:602`. **Neither file exists** - all six design notes were
absorbed and deleted in `28257e9` on 2026-08-08, one day before this bead's last edit. And the
position was reversed *in this bead's favour* on 2026-08-09: **D27** (`factory-loop.md:105`)
decides "thin engine: the catalog defines, the host executes... the host runtime spawns the
subagent, resolves its tier and fires the boundary hooks", and **D28** amends the Conductor
refusal because "both installed runtimes contradict it by construction".

**Its gating open question is now answered, and the answer changes the scope.** An externally
spawned process is always a separate session and can **never** appear as a subagent row inside
a live interactive session. Non-interactive host dispatch: yes. Nested in the driving session:
never. So the bead's own re-scope branch - the engine emits work a session executes - is a
genuinely different design that must be chosen deliberately rather than fallen into.

**The plan's justification for this row does not survive checking.**
`implementation-plan.md:225` says the question is "answered twice over", citing a competing
harness that "runs exactly this split in production". `factory-loop.md:1115` says that
harness's loop does **not** call any LLM and emits a prompt to stdout - which is an existence
proof for the re-scope branch, not for engine-driven host dispatch.

**The real content is the spawn mode**, and it is measured: `skills:` is honoured for a spawned
subagent and **not** under `claude --agent <name> -p`, this repo's only dispatch shape. That is
`basicly-ey58`, which this bead should depend on. One sub-claim below is also stale: `.claude/`
agents are no longer inert - `roles.py:93-105` stats them and `runner.py:547-570` injects
`--agent` - but **0 of 346 recorded dispatches carry it**, against a positive control of 163
carrying `-p`, so the effect is still nil.

The four non-negotiables below - D1's singleton supervisor, D9's `prompt_sha256`, metering, and
agnosticism as contract - are all still current and survive the restatement.

---

## Context

Every dispatch in this engine ends at one `subprocess.Popen` (`runner.py:1469`) of a CLI
binary — `("claude","-p",PROMPT)`, `("codex","exec",PROMPT)`, `("copilot","-p",PROMPT)`
(`runner.py:275-308`). **No code path anywhere asks the host to run a subagent.**

Measured 2026-08-08: flags actually passed are `--output-format`, `--verbose`,
`--forward-subagent-text`, `--session-id`, `--disallowedTools`, `--model`. **Zero hits**
for `--agents`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--permission-mode`, `--resume`.

And the agents we do project are inert: `.claude/agents/` holds three files written by
`agents.sync()`, and **no dispatch code reads that directory** — its only other consumer
is `cli.py:1261`, which globs it to *delete* files.

## The decision this contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident

`agent-roster-design.md:210` refuses this by name:

> role prompts *"cannot be Claude subagent files — the factory is agent-agnostic and
> dispatches headless Claude, Codex, and Copilot alike."*

And `factory-loop-requirements.md:602` treats host nesting as a **hazard** ("can fan out
inside itself, unmetered and outside the supervisor's model"), never a capability.

**Two measurements undercut the premise rather than the principle.** First, the
agnosticism is hollow in practice: of 338 run records, `claude` 156 and `manual` 182 —
**codex and copilot have zero dispatches, ever**, while the README advertises all three.
Second, D6's decisive row — light mode has *"one window shared by everything"*, therefore
*"light cannot replace dark"* (`factory-loop-requirements.md:629,634`) — is contradicted by
this repo's own measurement at `steering-surfaces-design.md:25`, which records a subagent
body as *"never enters the parent … low — isolated context"*. **Subagents are isolated, not
shared.** The stated reason for refusing host-native dispatch does not hold.

## What must survive any replacement

Not everything in D6 is refuted, and these are the non-negotiables:

- **D1's singleton deterministic supervisor** owning the base checkout and the serial merge
  queue (`factory-design.md:47-61`). A host fan-out must not become a second writer.
- **D9's prompt-hash reproducibility** — *"two runs of the same node are diffable"*
  (`factory-design.md:295`). `prompt_sha256` is already recorded and must stay meaningful.
- **Metering.** The hazard `flr:602` names is real: a host-spawned agent that fans out
  inside itself is invisible to `run-records.json`. Whatever replaces `-p` must record
  spend per unit of work or the spend ceiling (5 correct firings) stops working.
- **Agent-agnosticism as a contract**, even if unexercised: the host path must be one
  runner among several, not a hard dependency on Claude.

## Open question this bead must answer before it builds

Whether the host runtime can be driven **non-interactively from the engine** at all, or
only from a live session — because the supervisor is a subprocess, not a session. If only
the latter, this becomes "the engine emits work the session executes", which is a
different design and should be re-scoped rather than forced.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner host` completes a unit of work without spawning
`claude -p`, and `uv run basicly usage` shows its spend.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`
- depends on: none

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given a unit of work, when it is dispatched through the host runtime, then its spend is
  recorded in `run-records.json` exactly as a `-p` dispatch is - check: a test asserts a
  record with non-zero tokens and a `prompt_sha256` exists after a host dispatch.
- Given concurrent host dispatches, when they land, then the serial merge queue and the
  singleton supervisor lock still hold - check: a test asserts two host lanes cannot both
  write the base checkout.
- Given a repo whose configured runner is not claude, when a dispatch is requested, then
  the engine still dispatches - check: a test asserts the host path is one runner among
  several and does not become mandatory.

payload.value: A Claude lane dispatched through the host runtime records its spend in the run records exactly as a subprocess dispatch does, with a `prompt_sha256` present. Concurrent host dispatches still leave the singleton supervisor and the serial merge queue as the only writer of the base checkout. A repository configured for a non-Claude runner still dispatches, so the host path stays one runner among several rather than a hard dependency.

## Trigger

When the module-size waiver on `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` still names `basicly-kr7t` as its reason, I want to remove the waiver and bring the file under the 4,000-token cap, so I can close the debt the waiver stands in for.

## Context

`basicly-r343` fixed the schema scan and could not land without a size waiver. This bead removes that waiver by doing the work the waiver stands in for.

```text
.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py   6,554 frozen, 6,525 used   29 tokens of headroom
the r343 fix adds                829 tokens
now                            7,432 tokens               1.86 times the cap
```

## Why the waiver is not the right end state

`factory-loop.md` section 9.3 states that the first change to a frozen file **under 8,000 tokens** must bring it under the cap, not merely reduce it. This file was 6,554, so the recorded obligation was to extract.

A waiver is for a module that is genuinely cohesive. The `r343` implementer named a real seam in its own report and then waived on cost rather than on cohesion. It said so plainly, which is why this bead exists rather than a silent concession.

## The seam it named

The reference index is a nameable responsibility that does not import back: `_iter_files`, `_read`, `_dotted`, `Index` and `build_index`. It is about a 2,000-token move and it touches every function in the file plus `tests/test_verify.py`.

## Measure before you cut

The two size ratchets pull opposite ways. Extracting code raises the remaining prose share, so an extraction fixes both gates only when the extracted unit's prose share is above its origin's. Measure both with the gates' own scripts before choosing the cut.

## Acceptance

- When the extraction lands, then `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is under the 4,000-token cap.
- When the module-size gate runs, then the waiver count returns to 1 and the waiver comment is gone from the file.
- When `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` is read, then it no longer carries a module-size waiver delta.
- When the dead-code gate runs before and after, then it reports the same finding count.
- When both size gates run, then neither baseline is raised.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- a new module under `.scripts/`
- `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` reports the same count as before the split, and `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports one waiver rather than two.

## Trigger

When an agent has only the board and nothing else, I want it to answer all nine of the owner's operator questions and offer the verbs that change the flow of work, so I can see and control the loop without a session transcript.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05, restating a requirement they say they have given many times: *"the requirement was also to make the board interactive or a cockpit or a control panel where we can see and control the flow of work. Cool thing would be to be able to easily start, stop work, descope and so on."*

And the reason, in their words: *"One of the biggest issues with agentic development in the terminal alone is that human has no idea what is going on and when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried under. Terminal is fast and no one scrolls up, having multiple terminals does not help."*

And the test they set: *"if you as an agent look at the board, and only have access to the board, would you be able to see what is going on? what work is available, what work can start, is in progress? start work, stop work, inspect work (the info written in the record in a structured way)? descope work, scope work?"*

Explicitly **not** in scope: *"it is not about creating new records - that we can do via terminal. it is about work loop transparency and control."*

And the standing instruction: *"the board, even if it is a byproduct of basicly, it is essential and should grow with the basicly."*

## The gap, measured

Taken against the served board at 127.0.0.1:8788 on 2026-09-05, and against the snapshot it renders.

| the owner's question | answered today | by what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what work is available | partly | `NEXT UP` draws 3 of 234 ready |
| what can start now | yes | `THE QUEUE`: 262 needs nothing, 24 waits on one, 8 waits on a chain |
| what is in progress | yes | `RUNNING NOW` and `CLAIMED, NO LANE` |
| what is blocked, and by what | yes | `THE QUEUE` names the top blockers and the longest chain |
| **inspect one record** | **no** | `units[]` carries `id, phase, priority, ready, status, title, type` and no body |
| **start work** | **no** | no action offers `loop run` or `supervise` |
| **stop work** | partly | `lane-kill` is in `ACTIONS`, but only reachable when an ask prefills it |
| **descope / scope** | **no** | no action changes status or priority |
| when will it be done | no | `basicly-hymq99` and `basicly-w6vbw61` |

So four of nine. The two channels that are missing are **inspect** and **control**, and they are missing for different reasons.

## The seam already exists

`board_actions.ACTIONS` is a closed table of three argv builders handed to the installed CLI as a subprocess. Its docstring states the design: *"The board is a renderer with a keyboard."* `.importlinter`'s `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` contract holds because the board never reads the tracker; it runs `basicly`.

That is the answer to inspect as well as control. A record's body does not have to enter the snapshot - 294 bodies would be a snapshot nobody can serve. The board runs `basicly tracker show <id>` the same way it runs `basicly policy checkpoint`, and renders what comes back. No contract moves.

`board_asks.pending` already prefills a row per implementable offer. What is missing is a surface for an action that no *ask* proposes - a ready record has no ask, so today nothing offers to start it.

## Redefined by the owner, 2026-09-06 — the cockpit is a development environment

> *"the board is the human instrument for implementation of new features. the human will set
> up the backlog with the agent using terminal, and then it will view and control the
> implementation via the board. That is why this board design must look like a development
> environment for a human, where he sees what is going on and can react on it."*

And the reason, which is the same one they have given all session in different words:

> *"I have asked you many times during implementation, and several times in this session,
> where are we now. that is because I cannot see clearly where we are."*

**This supersedes the wall framing.** The board was built as a glance surface read from across
a room, and every design decision followed from that: cap the lists, prefer counts to members,
draw a diagram rather than a backlog. Those were right for a wall and are wrong for a cockpit.
`basicly-a68ggd` is the clearest case - it is closed, and its title is *"the loop region shows
the whole backlog binned by phase instead of the running pass"*. The region was deliberately
made **not** a list of what sits in each phase. The owner is now asking for exactly that list.
It is a reversal on a new requirement, not a regression, and it is recorded here so nobody
re-closes `a68ggd`'s finding on top of it.

**The division of labour, stated by the owner:** the backlog is set up *with an agent in the
terminal*. The cockpit is where a human **views and controls the implementation**. So the
cockpit does not need record creation - it needs seeing and reacting.

**Two surfaces, not one page:**

1. **The loop** - what is happening now, as a kanban of phase columns in the shape Linear and
   Jira use, where each phase names its members and a member is reachable.
2. **The backlog** - what is planned, ordered, with the controls to shape it.

**Titles carry the meaning, ids are the address.** The owner: *"the real titles of features and
tasks are more important than IDs. IDs should be there but focus is on titles, description,
priority, and dependency."* The board leads with ids in most regions today.

**And the case nothing is designed for: N sessions on one repository.** The owner:
*"4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."* Shared
branch, shared worktrees. `basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped worktree visibility, which is one agent's
answer to "who is inside a lane"; it says nothing about which *session* holds what, whether two
are about to collide, or what a fifth terminal joining should be told.

**Priority:** the owner has made visualization number one, on the ground that the cockpit is
*"the 1st thing a user will see when starting basicly after installation in their repo"*.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- children decompose this; each is a leaf a lane can build

Every capability stays an argv handed to the installed CLI, so `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` still holds.

## Trigger

When the quality-gate guidance says only to run the repository's checks, I want it to name the one command that runs every gate and the pass line to confirm, so I can stop a hand-picked subset from being reported as the whole gate.

## Context

Session 2026-08-14, and this is a user-visible mistake rather than a near miss: I reported "all
gates green" before committing `basicly-ejdm.2`, then the commit was **refused**. What I had run
was `pytest` plus five checker scripts I picked by name. What I had not run was the gate, which
then failed on `pyright` and `projection-skills`.

The `quality-gate` fragment says: *"Run the repo's checks on anything touched, re-run after the
final edit"*, and *"Point at gates, don't restate them."*

## Root cause, and it is in the wording

"The repo's checks" is a **set an agent has to assemble**, and an agent that has just run five
checkers has evidence it assembled it correctly. There is no moment at which a hand-picked subset
announces that it is a subset - it looks exactly like the whole.

The repo already has the one command: `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` runs all 20 and prints
`checks passed: 20/20`. Nothing in the guidance names it, so the fragment describes an outcome
where it could name a command - which is the inversion of section 3.1, the rule that guidance
points at the enforcement rather than restating it.

## Proposed change, for a human to apply

Amend the `quality-gate` fragment so the check step **names the command** rather than the set:
run the repo's own gate runner, and confirm the pass line it prints. The count in that line is
what makes a subset visible - `18/20` cannot be misread as green, while five green scripts can.

D25 forbids an agent amending the catalog, so this is filed rather than applied.

## The second half, which the wording cannot fix

I also reported the result before running the gate. The fragment already carries
*"Confirm success from the explicit pass/fail summary line; truncated output hides failures"* -
that rule was right and I did not follow it. Only the first half is a guidance defect.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The `quality-gate` fragment's check step must name the command that runs every gate, not describe a set an agent assembles itself. The fragment must name the exact pass-line format to confirm, such as a count of checks passed against the total.

## Trigger

When a pass changes nothing and re-dispatches a decider for an item a human already routed, I want the supervisor to stop re-deciding it and end the session with a stalled narrative, so I can stop paying for identical passes that buy no progress.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly loop supervise basicly-zq9i2m --tier high --max-passes 8`. Passes 4 to 8 were identical: `carried: basicly-2kh170 - landing without a new dispatch`, then `routed: basicly-2kh170 -> rework` on the same scope collision, then the pass spend gate refused (`89259646 tokens forecast; 87452222 remaining`), then `decider: basicly-zq9i2m#3018546b66 [escalation] to human` with a fresh decider rendering each time. The ledger holds 5 `[harness-run] phase=decide` records for that one decision id. Nothing changed between the passes: no lane dispatched, no landing succeeded, the queue held the same item. The session ended `stopped: --max-passes 8 reached`, so five of eight passes bought nothing and the operator read a full pass count as work.

Two defects share the root that a pass has no notion of "this pass changed nothing":

1. `record_pass_refusal` is idempotent per (issue, kind, question), so the queue item was correctly re-enqueued once, but the decider was dispatched again on every pass for an item it had already routed to a human. A human-routed item is pending until a human answers; re-deciding it spends a decider run per pass and cannot change the answer.
2. A pass whose only outcomes are a repeated landing refusal and a repeated queue item is a stall. The supervisor kept looping until `--max-passes`, and a session without that flag would loop until the operator noticed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Root with one carried lane whose landing bounces on a stable cause (a scope collision with a live sibling), and ready children whose forecast exceeds the remaining grant. `basicly loop supervise <root> --max-passes 4`. Observed: 4 identical passes, 4 decider runs on one decision id. Expected: after the first pass that changes nothing, the session ends with a `stalled:` narrative naming the pending decision and the bounced lane, and the decider runs at most once per queue item.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: When the next pass finds a queue item the decider already routed to a human still pending, no new decider dispatch must run for it, and the pass narrative must name it as pending on a human. When a pass dispatches no lane, lands no lane, and enqueues no new item, the supervisor must end the session with a stalled narrative naming every pending item and bounced lane, and exit non-zero. When a pass dispatches or lands at least one lane, the session must continue as today.

When a suppression list cites the wrong file or carries a stale hit count, I want each citation to resolve to its suppressed condition and each count checked for staleness, so I can trust the exemption tables instead of auditing the wrong module.

## Context

Found by the lane-E cross-cutting survey 2026-08-14. Three defects in the lists' own claims, each verified.

```text
pyproject.toml:90   says the two false positives sit at hooks.py:280 and :282
                    they are at precommit_config.py:127 and :129
                    hooks.py:280 is now a different function
pyproject.toml      says two of them are true false positives
                    a third is: tb, a protocol parameter at tracker_usage.py:286
.ruff.toml          records 111 hits for one ignored rule
                    measured today: 187
```

A maintainer who follows the first citation audits the wrong module.

The rule with the stale count keeps its rationale, which survives. What rots is the number, and nothing ratchets the growth of an ignored family. A second recorded count still measures correctly, so the rot is per entry rather than systemic.

## A fourth of the same class

`tracker_surface.py:51` points at a function in `tracker_usage`. The function lives in `tracker_invocation.py:62`. And `tracker_surface.py:52` re-spells a constant from `tracker_invocation.py:30`. The concept a token that can be a tracker surface word has two definitions.

## Re-measured 2026-08-19, two of the four halves are moot

Two files this record named do not exist: a tracker surface module and a tracker invocation module. So the finding that two definitions of the surface-word concept had drifted apart is **gone with the modules**, and two of the four declared scope entries went with it.

What survives is the suppression-list half, and it is still live: the project file cites a hook module for names that live elsewhere, and the lint configuration carries a count that no longer matches its population.

This is one instance of a general rule filed as `basicly-twfj` and re-measured under `basicly-e2mz.48.2`: every exemption list is machine validated against the population it exempts from. Five of this repository's exemption tables already report a stale entry and several do not. Prefer folding this record into that work over fixing two citations by hand, because the hand fix leaves the next drift undetected.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml`
- `.ruff.toml`
