## Trigger

When `basicly verify` only accepts `--mode` and cannot run one declared check by name, I want a `--only` option that runs exactly one declared check with its declared argv, so I can stop hand-rolling a check's argv and reporting a false finding.

## Retro proposal, not applied

Session 2026-09-12. Awaiting the owner decision; a retro finding is never self-applied.

## The incident, twice in one session
Asked whether the bandit gate covers `packages/`, I ran `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r src .scripts packages` and reported a failure. The declared check is `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r .scripts .basicly/core/hooks .basicly/core/kit`. My invented path list produced a finding the real gate does not have, and I retracted it.

The same shape had already happened with the kits: `uv run --project packages/basicly-tier` reported all three kits broken, because that path reads the source tree where `force-include` has not run. Also retracted.

## Root cause, and why it is not a discipline failure
There is no way to run one declared check. `basicly verify` takes `--mode`, not a check name, so the only route to "run just this gate" is to retype its argv from `basicly.toml` - or, as happened, to approximate it.

Measured on `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json`: `bandit` 19 direct invocations, `vulture` 67, `pyright` 267, `lint-imports` 140. `verify` appears once. The tools are run directly essentially always, and every direct run is an argv nobody checked against the declared one.

The `core-rules` fragment already says the authority is the code that reads it, not the docs. The authority here is `basicly.toml`, and the harness offers no way to obey it.

## Proposal
`basicly verify --only <name>` runs exactly one `[[verify.checks]]` entry with its declared argv, and refuses an unknown name by listing the ones that exist.

## Why this rather than a hook
A guard on hand-rolled invocations would fire on 493 recorded calls, most of them legitimate narrowing. The cheaper fix is to make the correct path exist, so the improvisation has a named alternative.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: `basicly verify --only` shall run exactly the argv declared for the named `[[verify.checks]]` entry in `basicly.toml`. An unknown check name shall be refused with a list of the names that exist. The command shall exit with the check's own exit code.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] `basicly verify --only bandit` runs exactly the argv declared for the `bandit` entry in `basicly.toml`.
- [ ] `basicly verify --only` with an unknown name refuses and lists the known check names.
- [ ] The command's exit code matches the underlying check's exit code.
- [ ] A test in `tests/test_verify.py` asserts both the correct-name and unknown-name paths.

## Trigger

When the plan's section 5.2 row 11 asks for evidence on the `chars/4` token estimator, and two measurements disagree in an informative way, I want that band recorded where a test can check it, so I can back the plan's evidence claim without re-arguing the measurement.

## Context

Replaces the remedy `basicly-ca42` was building. The owner decided on 2026-08-13 to keep
`chars/4`, so `ca42` is parked (`deferred`) and its branch `harness/basicly-ca42` is not
landing.

What the plan's section 5.2 row 11 originally asked for was evidence, and two measurements
now exist and disagree in an informative way.

`basicly-u2hl.32` measured `chars/4` against tiktoken `o200k_base` per population:

```text
prose (skill bodies)              +1.6%
beads issue json                 -10.7%
run-record json                  -16.4%
run-record markdown headings     -28.9%
run-record tsv                   -39.5%
```

`basicly-ca42` then measured Python source directly: 444,810 real against 453,800 estimated,
so `chars/4` is 2.02% **over** on code - refuting the bead's own prediction that code, being
structured text, would sit in the 10-40% under-counting band.

So the estimator is accurate on the populations the factory actually denominates in code and
prose, and badly wrong on serialized records. That is a narrower and better-supported claim
than either bead made alone, and it is the claim the docstring should carry.

## Proposed check

`read_cost.py`'s docstring records both measurements with their populations and dates, and
the prohibition from `basicly-u2hl.32` on the one use the unit cannot support is retained
and named. A test asserts the recorded band matches a re-measurement on the fixtures.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The measured accuracy band per population and the two measurement dates shall be recorded in a test name or a README, not a code comment or docstring. The prohibition on using `chars/4` for the one population it cannot support (serialized records) shall be named alongside the band. A test shall assert the recorded band matches a re-measurement on the fixtures.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] A test module or README states the measured `chars/4` accuracy band per population, with the two measurement dates.
- [ ] The prohibition on using `chars/4` for serialized-record token counts is named alongside the band.
- [ ] A test re-measures the fixtures and asserts the result matches the recorded band.
- [ ] No docstring or prose comment is added to `read_cost.py` to carry this fact.

## Trigger

When a board serve test fails about once with `served is not None` false, but repeat runs reproduce nothing, I want the test to print the board's failure state and the holder age at the point of failure, so I can find the real cause instead of guessing from one run.

## Observation
`tests/test_board_serve.py::test_a_stale_lock_hands_the_fold_back_to_the_viewer` failed inside the pre-push suite on 2026-09-12, refusing a docs-only push. The full suite had passed minutes earlier on the same tree.

```
assert None is not None
tests/test_board_serve.py:218: AssertionError
```

Line 218 is `assert served is not None`. Lines 215 and 216 passed, so `board.refresh()` had returned True and `board.refreshes` was 1.

## Not reproduced
Three runs of the test alone: pass. Three runs of the whole file under `-n 8`: 27 passed each time. Six attempts, zero reproductions.

## Hypothesis ruled out, recorded so nobody spends the same hour
The obvious read is a race between the two independent `live_holder` calls: `refresh` proceeds only when the holder is not live, and `payload` returns `_served` only when the holder is not live, otherwise reading a snapshot file that may not exist. That would explain a None.

It cannot happen. `live_holder` returns None once `age_s >= STALE_AFTER_S`, the test ages the lock to `STALE_AFTER_S + 1`, and an age only grows. The holder cannot become live between the two calls.

So `payload` returned `_served` and `_served` was None, while `refresh` had returned True on the branch that assigns it. Those two statements cannot both be true of one object, which is why this needs an instrument rather than another read.

## Suggested first step
Have the test print `board.failures`, `board._served is None` and the holder age at the point of failure, then leave it in the suite until it fires again. A cause guessed without a second observation is a guess.

## Why it matters
The pre-push suite is the gate before every push. A test that fails about once refuses work that is fine and trains people to re-run rather than read. This is the second timing-dependent test in this file: `basicly-gssz1qa` fixed a different one on 2026-09-12, which compared two pages against the clock.

## Scope
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The test shall print `board.failures`, whether `board._served` is None, and the holder age at the point of failure, and stay in the suite until it fires again. The already-ruled-out `live_holder` race hypothesis shall not be re-investigated without new evidence. Once the instrumented failure is captured, the real cause shall be fixed with a regression test.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] `test_a_stale_lock_hands_the_fold_back_to_the_viewer` prints `board.failures`, `board._served is None`, and the holder age when the assertion fails.
- [ ] The instrumentation stays in the test until the failure is captured at least once more.
- [ ] Once captured, the record names the real cause, distinct from the ruled-out `live_holder` race.
- [ ] A regression test pins the fix so the flake does not return.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When an agent declares a model tier and the host is Claude or Copilot, I want the spawned subagent to run on the model that tier resolves to on that host, so I can rely on a declared tier on both hosts the owner scoped in.

## Context

Filed 2026-07-31 after basicly-kjc5.58 landed. **Re-scoped the same day by the owner, who was right and
the first framing was wrong**: this is NOT claude-only. GitHub Copilot custom agents carry a per-agent
`model` field too, so at least claude AND copilot must be supported. Re-verified against live
authoritative docs rather than recall.

basicly-kjc5.59 is the resolution seam but its scope is `runner.py`/`run_record.py`/`config.py` - the
HEADLESS runner dispatch path, where a model is set by `_apply_model` via a `--model` flag or a
`{model}` placeholder. A natively spawned subagent never goes through that path: the host reads a
per-agent file and takes the model from frontmatter. basicly-kjc5.58 removed that line for every
family, so a declared tier is currently decorative for every natively spawned agent.

Concrete regression from kjc5.58, deliberate and known: the shipped `test-runner` declared
`model: haiku`, now declares `tier: low`, and `.claude/agents/test-runner.md` carries no model line, so
an agent whose own prose says "cheap and fast on purpose" inherits the session model on every spawn.
Verified: `rg '^model' .claude/agents/` matches nothing.

kjc5.58 was still right - the defect was a NON-PORTABLE value in a family-agnostic source. The fix is
to emit the resolved per-surface spelling, which is what basicly-kjc5.61's map must provide.

## Verified facts (live docs, 2026-07-31)

- **Claude Code** reads `.claude/agents/<slug>.md`; `model` takes a hyphenated id (`claude-haiku-4-5`)
  or a short alias (`haiku`), or `inherit`.
- **GitHub Copilot** custom agents live at `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` (org/enterprise: root
  `agents/`). Frontmatter: `description` (required), `name`, `target` (`vscode`|`github-copilot`),
  `tools`, `model`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `mcp-servers`, `metadata`; body
  capped at 30000 chars, which `agents.MAX_BODY_CHARS` already matches.
- **Copilot's `model` value is a DISPLAY NAME**, not an id - `Claude Opus 4.5`, `Claude Sonnet 4` -
  and it accepts **a single string OR a prioritized array** tried in order
  (`model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2']`). Our schema cannot express an ordered fallback list today.
- **VS Code reads BOTH** `.github/agents` and `.claude/agents` ("VS Code also detects `.md` files in the
  `.claude/agents` folder, following the Claude sub-agents format"). So basicly-ajq's rationale holds
  for VS Code but NOT for the Copilot cloud agent or Copilot CLI, which do not read `.claude/agents`.
- Copilot `tools` names differ from Claude's and are inconsistent across sources
  (`["read","search","edit"]` in the VS Code doc vs `codebase`/`terminal`/`edit`/`github` elsewhere), so
  a copilot projection needs a pinned tool-name mapping, not a copy.

## Prerequisite

The copilot half has no target file today: basicly still projects to `.claude/agents` only. Reopening
that is filed separately and must land first for the copilot half. The claude half is unblocked once
kjc5.61 lands.

## Open design decision for the owner

Per surface, either resolve the tier to that surface's own spelling and emit it, or emit nothing and
record that the tier was not honoured (the stance kjc5.59 already takes where a family has no slot).
Recommendation: resolve and emit wherever the surface has a model slot, because that is the only case
in which the tier vocabulary changes real behaviour instead of documenting an intention.

Scope: `src/basicly/agents.py`, `.claude/agents/`, `tests/test_agents.py`.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: On Claude, a spawned subagent runs on the model its declared tier resolves to, with no model line in any projected agent file. On Copilot, the tier reaches the per-subagent config that basicly-u2hl.41 builds. A tier the map cannot resolve for a host is refused, and the refusal names the agent, the host and the tier.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The rule returns the repository pyz when present, else a vendored kit folder, else basicly-tracker on PATH.
- [ ] The claim hook and the standalone commit-msg hook call the rule.
- [ ] When the repository has a ledger and the rule finds no tracker at the pinned version, the commit is refused with the install command, never skipped.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a hook, the board or an agent needs the tracker, I want one resolution rule that finds the repository tracker.pyz first and the user-level basicly-tracker second, so I can move the code out of the repository without each caller guessing.

## Context

Today .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-claim.py and the standalone commit-msg hook look only for .basicly/kit/tracker/cli.py. The existing vendored folder stays a valid third place for repositories installed before this change.
payload.requirements: The claim gate cannot turn off because the code moved; one rule, one place.
payload.title: resolve the tracker from the repository pyz or the user install through one rule

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] basicly-tracker init --user writes the tracker skill to the user skill roots, naming basicly-tracker with the ledger path.
- [ ] The skill states it applies only in a repository that holds .basicly/ledger.
- [ ] A repository skill of the same name still wins, and skills-check reports the shadow.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When the tracker code is installed once per machine, I want its skill installed once per user and correct in every repository, so I can let an agent find the tracker without a skill copy in each repository.

## Context

The kit skill writes python3 .basicly/kit/tracker/cli.py into the repository. A user-level skill loads in every repository, so it must say it applies only where .basicly/ledger exists, and fit the 200-token listing budget skills-user enforces.
payload.requirements: An agent in any repository with a ledger gets one correct command, and in a repository without one it is not prompted.
payload.title: install the tracker and board skills once per user

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] basicly-tracker init writes no kit code and refuses, with the install command, when no user-level tracker is on PATH.
- [ ] basicly-tracker init --sandbox writes .basicly/tracker.pyz and a repository skill that names it.
- [ ] Switching a repository from one mode to the other with init leaves one mode's files, not both.
- [ ] The board kit init offers the same two modes.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a person sets up the tracker in a repository, I want the default to write only the ledger, the pin, the git rules and the hook, and a sandbox flag to vendor tracker.pyz and board.pyz instead, so I can choose shared or isolated with one flag and no manual steps.

## Context

basicly-tracker bundle already writes a 356 KB pyz that runs with plain python3. Today init vendors a 36-file, 936 KB folder.
payload.requirements: Two modes, one flag between them, and the ledger and its rules identical in both.
payload.title: give init a default machine mode and a sandbox mode that vendors one file

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] basicly-tracker update --sandbox replaces the folder with tracker.pyz and keeps the ledger byte-identical.
- [ ] basicly-tracker update in the default mode removes the folder only when a user-level tracker at the pin is on PATH.
- [ ] The claim and identity gates pass on the migration commit.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a repository already vendors .basicly/kit/tracker, I want update to move it to the default or the sandbox mode, so I can adopt the new layout without deleting files by hand.

## Context

Repositories such as terminal install the 36-file folder today. The folder keeps working through the resolution rule until it is migrated.
payload.requirements: A migration never changes ledger content and never leaves a repository without a working tracker.
payload.title: migrate a repository from the vendored kit folder to the new modes
